$comment: Small choices about mail, work, seats and incidents put to the decision model: a label at sharpAt or more is acted on, anything less keeps the room's own rule. deadlineMs: how long a call may take. Empty criteria: the labels come with the call. escalate.signals: the subjects it reads. policy.jev.forks lists the forks that are on.

question.instructions: `report` is the last message a software agent wrote when its turn of work ended, with no protocol word on its first line; `woke_by` are the subjects of the mail that started that turn. The agent's owner reads it. Say what the report brings its owner.

criteria.result: a result, a finding, a finished piece of work or a change of plan the owner should act on
criteria.question: a question, a request, a problem or a blocker that needs the owner
criteria.nothing_new: an acknowledgement, a repeat, or progress with nothing for the owner to act on

question.instructions: `subject` and `body` are a mail one software agent sent another that is idle. Say what the mail asks of its reader.

criteria.act: to do, change, check, decide or answer something
criteria.nothing: nothing: it only informs, and can wait for the reader's next mail

question.instructions: `error` is what an AI coding agent's program reported when a turn of its work failed. Say what kind of failure it is.

criteria.limited: a rate limit, a quota, or a usage or spending limit that lifts with time
criteria.fatal: a refused account or key, billing, or a prompt too long for the model: trying again changes nothing
criteria.service: a passing fault of the service or the network: trying again soon may work

question.instructions: `reply` is a mail that answers one of the questions in `asks`, sent by the agent the questions were asked of; it names none of them. Say which one it answers.
`pairs.{{id}}.a` and `pairs.{{id}}.b` are the write scopes of two tasks in one code base: what each task may change, said in words. Would doing both tasks at once change the same files?

criteria.true: they name the same files, module or feature
criteria.false: they touch different parts of the code

question.instructions: `title`, `spec` and `brief` say what a software agent is about to be started on. The labels are the models it may run on, each with what it is for. Say which model fits the work.
`issue` is a piece of work a software agent has just taken: its title, description, acceptance criteria and write scope. Say what it lacks before the agent can build it.

criteria.ready: nothing: it says what is wanted and what the result must satisfy
criteria.unclear: what is wanted can be read more than one way, or rests on facts the agent must find out first
criteria.no-acceptance: what is wanted is clear, but nothing says how to tell it is done
criteria.needs-decision: someone with authority must choose between ways before any work can start
criteria.too-big: it holds several independent pieces of work, more than one agent should carry

question.instructions: `message` is a mail a software agent sent its Owner, the seat directly above it, because it is blocked, has a question or needs a decision. Say who must answer it.

criteria.above: its Owner cannot settle it alone: it reaches past the Owner's own work, and the seat above the Owner must answer
criteria.room: the cause is a fault of the room itself, its tools, mail, limits or settings, not of the work
criteria.person: only a person can decide it: money, scope, direction, access, or a rule the seats may not change

question.instructions: `new` holds issues just made and `open` issues still open, each by id; the labels name the open ones. Say which open issue asks for the same work as the new issue {{id}}, or none.
`incidents.{{id}}` is a line from the log of a program that runs software agents: `district` is the part of the program that wrote it, `seen` how often. Say what would answer it.

criteria.tunable: a number or switch in the program's settings: a limit too low, a keep too short, a wait too small, a threshold too tight
criteria.code: a fault in the program's own code: an error it should not make, a case it does not handle, a state it cannot recover from
criteria.outside: a service or machine outside the program is down, slow or refusing: the network, a model provider, the agent app, the disk
